newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends down despite light buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends down despite light buying.

text.p: Rubber futures closed easier on Tuesday despite shortcovering by local manufacturers for RSS3 and RSS1 rubber in the local exchange, dealers said.

Volume in the local market bounced back from yesterday's meagre level of 275 tonnes. Volume for the January RSS3 contract here reached 715 tonnes while 750 tonnes was sold in the April/June RSS1 contract.
"The manufacturers involved in the purchase managed to get a really low price for the rubber. There were a lot of sellers offering rubber, but there were simply no takers," a rubber trader said.
"Most of the shortcovering was for RSS1 rubber. The manufacturer managed to get the rubber for a low price," a rubber trader said.

Total volume of RSS1 rubber traded in the local exchange reach an estimated 2,000-2,200 tonnes, dealers said. At around 0945 GMT, January RSS3 was seen at 124.25-124.50 U.S. cents a kg from Monday's settlement of 124.75 cents a kg.

January RSS1 was seen at 176.50-178.50 Singapore cents (US$1.26-$1.27) a kg from 178.50 cents. February TSR20 was seen at 172.00-174.00 Singapore cents (US$1.23-$1.24) a kg from 174.50 cents. (US$1-S$1.40) -- Rene Pastor (65-870-3305)
